name: rare-odds-collision

finding.title: Two concurrent `WriteReport` calls can share a temporary file and write one report's bytes into another
finding.description: `WriteReport` names its temporary file from `randomSuffix`. When two goroutines write reports in the same directory at once and `randomSuffix` returns the same value for both, both calls write the same `.report-` file, and one `os.Rename` moves the other report's bytes over its own path. That report's data is lost.

checks: export/report.go:14 names the temporary file from `randomSuffix` alone

finding.suggestedFix: Create the temporary file with `os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), ".report-*")`, which fails rather than reuse an existing name.

prDiff:
diff --git a/export/report.go b/export/report.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..2222222
--- /dev/null
+++ b/export/report.go
@@ -0,0 +1,26 @@
+package export
+
+import (
+	"crypto/rand"
+	"encoding/hex"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+)
+
+// WriteReport writes data to path through a temporary file in the same directory,
+// so a reader never sees a half-written report. Reports are written from many
+// goroutines at once.
+func WriteReport(path string, data []byte) error {
+	tmp := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(path), ".report-"+randomSuffix())
+	if err := os.WriteFile(tmp, data, 0o644); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	return os.Rename(tmp, path)
+}
+
+// randomSuffix returns 16 random bytes from crypto/rand as 32 hex characters.
+func randomSuffix() string {
+	b := make([]byte, 16)
+	_, _ = rand.Read(b)
+	return hex.EncodeToString(b)
+}
